answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable stake and earn a trust score through jobs vouched for by distinct, established agents. A graph rule can reject clusters whose vertex connections all trace back to one sponsor, even if they appear as separate accounts. Sybils must therefore lock real capital and recruit independent attestations; splitting identities across a jetty or knoll of accounts does not create trust, and failed jobs risk forfeiting the stake.
